name: actions-style-hermes
match_prompt:
You are judging a single match in a code-style tournament whose goal is to homogenize conventions across `app/actions/*.ts` (Next.js server actions).

Your match label: {LABEL}
Number of inputs: {N_INPUTS}

### Tools
You have EXACTLY two tools:
  - read_file(path) — read a file from disk
  - pick_winner(winner_id, reasoning, markdown) — declare which input wins (1 or 2), give a short reasoning, submit a synthesis markdown, and STOP.
No shell, no web, no edit, no write, no browser.

### Inputs
{INPUTS}

### Task
Read each input fully via read_file. Decide which input has the better conventions to model future code on (more consistent, more idiomatic, safer error handling, clearer auth boundaries, etc.). Then call pick_winner with:
  - winner_id: 1 or 2 — the position of the chosen input above
  - reasoning: 1–3 sentences naming the decisive factor(s)
  - markdown: a synthesis containing EXACTLY these section headers, in this order:

```
# Match {LABEL} — <short title>

## Shared patterns
- ...

## Divergent patterns
- ...

## Naming & exports
- ...

## Validation
- ...

## Error handling
- ...

## Auth & session
- ...

## Return shapes
- ...

## Database access
- ...

## Other conventions
- ...

## Guideline candidates
1. ...
2. ...
```

After calling pick_winner, STOP — do not emit further text or tool calls.

Constraints:
- Under 500 words inside the markdown.
- The synthesis must stand alone — downstream rounds will NOT see the original files, only this markdown.
- Identify 5–12 prescriptive, testable guideline candidates.
- Be concrete (quote short identifiers when useful) but don't paste whole functions.
- Your guideline candidates should reflect the WINNER's conventions, citing the loser only to contrast.
